label: <DEL> step of long (L=8-9) sequences with a specific y/p/2/k/v...x token template
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.003% of steps). All of its activation falls on the delimiter step (phase 1, recall_idx 0), and almost only in long sequences: L=9 holds 70% of the mass, L=8 holds 29%, L=7 has 2 hits, and it never fires for L<=6, on original-phase steps, or on copy steps. Within that slot it behaves like a soft template match on the original sequence: first token y (60% of mass; g/p add a little), p or 2 in positions 1-2, k/v around position 3, and x as the last original token (prev_tok x, 42% of mass). The max example y p 2 k v a s x <DEL> matches all of these. A count of at least 3 of these 5 cues on L>=8 delimiter steps gives dev F1 0.31 (precision 0.24, mass recall 0.56). Loosening to 2 cues reaches 0.90 mass recall, but precision falls to 0.03. Many activations only partly match the template (e.g. p k k k t q c f f), so the boundary is graded and not captured cleanly. Magnitude seems to rise with the number of cues matched, but I only checked this from the top examples.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=1 & out_tok=y (+3.93), orig2=k (+2.77), orig2=2 (+2.61), orig3=k (+2.19), phase=1 & out_tok=p (+2.00), phase=1 & out_tok=g (+1.98). Lower it: orig7=- (-3.06), in_first=0 (-2.64), in_count=1 (-1.70), out_tok=- (-1.40).
